newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Optus says mobile revenue soars.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Optus says mobile revenue soars.

text.p: Optus Communications Pty Ltd, the nation's second telecoms carrier, said it achieved a 58 percent rise in mobile phone revenues during the 1996/97 first half, the strongest gain of its three divisions.

The company, which is 25 percent owned by Mayne Nickless Ltd, said mobile services revenue rose to A$530 million while long distance sales rose 24 per cent to A$476 million and business network services revenue rose 35 percent to A$144 million.

Its share of the long distance market at the end of December 1996 was 18 percent, with a 32 percent share of the total mobile market which included 37 percent of the mobile digital market and 28 percent of the mobile analogue market.
Pre-tax earnings in the six months to December 31 jumped to A$59 million from A$7 million a year ago. Revenue rose by A$288 million or 32 percent to A$1.195 billion.
"These achievements give Optus a very strong platform for continued growth in the deregulated environment, which will begin in July 1997," Optus chief executive Ziggy Switkowski said.

Optus will compete directly with the Australian government-owned market leader Telstra Corp from the second half of calendar 1997. One-third of Telstra is due to be floated by the government in the next two years, while a float of the Optus stake held by Mayne Nickless has been delayed due to legal proceedings with pay television affiliate Optus Vision and Seven Network Ltd.

"The deregulated environment will have its challenges, most importantly the need to stimulate competition at a wholesale as well as a retail level, but Optus is good overcoming challenges," Switkowski said.
"This is clearly evident in the positive results achieved in the half to December 1996."
The other major shareholders in Optus are BellSouth Corp and Cable and Wireless Plc each with 24.5 percent.
